profile.name: Javed Qadir Bakhsh
profile.headline: A life of public service, Christian leadership, and preservation of history
introduction: Javed Qadir Bakhsh is a Pakistani public servant, Christian leader, Formanite, and historian whose life has been shaped by three enduring commitments: service to the nation, service to the Church, and preservation of history for future generations.

His journey encompasses Christian student leadership, a distinguished career in the Government of Pakistan, international professional training, and decades of active participation in the life and administration of the Church of Pakistan.

In 1962, following his father’s transfer from Christ Church, Drigh Road, Karachi, to the Central Cathedral of Praying Hands, Lahore, he moved to Lahore with his family and was admitted to Cathedral School, Hall Road. He completed his Matriculation in 1969.
profile.guidingPrinciple: Preserve history for the coming generations.
profile.conviction: Service is a responsibility, and history is a legacy.

education.title: Forman Christian College · the beginning of leadership
body: He is a Formanite, having graduated from Forman Christian College, Lahore, in 1974, and completed postgraduate studies in 1976.

During his student years he was actively involved in the Student Christian Movement (SCM) and served as General Secretary of the Student Christian Movement and as Student Secretary of the National Student Christian Movement.

publicService.title: Public service to Pakistan
body: After completing his education, he entered the Government of Pakistan and pursued a career devoted to public service.
He ultimately served as Joint Census Commissioner, Government of Pakistan, contributing to the country’s national census and demographic administration.
In 1989 he earned a scholarship under the Bush Scholarship programme and travelled to the United States for professional training at the U.S. Census Bureau in Washington, D.C.

He was in charge of the Population Census Organization for Punjab province and also headed the Coordination Department in Islamabad, with extensive experience of field operations in Pakistan’s largest data-collection and analysis agency.

churchService.title: Service to the Church of Pakistan
churchService.intro: Alongside his government career, he remained deeply involved in the life and administration of the Church of Pakistan at parish, diocesan, and national levels.
roles: Executive Committee (Church of Pakistan) · member, participating in administration and affairs of the united Church
Parish Committee · member, contributing to parish administration and community life
Clergy Ordination Committee (Diocese of Raiwind) · member, contributing to matters concerning candidates for ordained ministry
Education Board · member, reflecting continuing interest in Christian education and institutional development

historyMission.title: A passion for Church history
body: A defining feature of his continuing work is preserving the history of the Church of Pakistan and the Christian community in Pakistan · documenting the formation and development of the Church, its dioceses, bishops, clergy, lay leaders, and institutions.
He believes history is the collective memory of a community, and that the contributions of clergy, lay people, students, and Christian institutions should be recorded so they are not lost.
His historical work includes preserving the life and legacy of his father, Bishop Johnston Safdar Qadir Bakhsh, a pioneering leader of the Church of Pakistan.

digitalWork.title: History: Church of Pakistan · digital work
body: He created the Facebook page “History: Church of Pakistan,” sharing photographs and memories of clergy, lay leaders, and others who have served the Church, and facts from official minutes and records.

He also initiated two Facebook programmes: Rab Ki Khidmat (Service of the Spirit) · focusing on faith, Christian service, and spiritual encouragement; and Motivational Programmes for Youngsters · to encourage and inspire young people in personal, professional, and spiritual journeys.
As part of the motivational programme, he would like to interview young professionals and successful young Pakistanis so they can share experiences, challenges, achievements, and lessons learned.
His vision is to preserve the past, celebrate those who served, and inspire the younger generation to build a better future.

legacy.title: Legacy and continuing mission
legacy.body: His continuing mission is to ensure that the history of Christian institutions and communities in Pakistan is recorded, preserved, and made available to future generations · bringing together people, places, institutions, documents, photographs, memories, Church records, and personal testimonies.
